newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy aims for PLO-Israel meeting this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy aims for PLO-Israel meeting this week.

text.p: A U.S. Middle East envoy wants to arrange a "probing meeting" of Israelis and Palestinians to try to break a two-month-old deadlock in peacemaking, PLO and Western officials said on Sunday.
But the two sides could not even agree on the issues to be discussed.
Talks are stuck over Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu's building of a Jewish settlement in disputed Jerusalem and an Israeli demand for a PLO crackdown on "terrorism".

The envoy, Dennis Ross, returned to Jerusalem from Cairo on Saturday after meeting Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak. PLO officials said he would meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat at 10 p.m. (1900 GMT) in the West Bank city of Ramallah.
"Ross presented some ideas on how to restart contacts with Israel," a PLO official said.

"He suggested a meeting, not negotiations, between PLO and Israeli negotiators attended by Ross himself to probe into the issues that led to the crisis in the peace talks," said the official, who declined to be identified.
"Those issues are Israeli settlement activities including Jabal Abu Ghneim and Israeli violations in occupied Jerusalem."

Netanyahu started work in March on the 6,500-unit Har Homa Jewish settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim, a hilltop in Arab East Jerusalem, occupied in 1967 and later annexed by Israel. Both sides claim Jerusalem.

Western officials said Ross was awaiting a response from Arafat on whether Palestinians would meet the Israelis on the issues that led to the talks breakdown. Arafat met his negotiating team in Ramallah on Saturday night.

Officials said the PLO was willing to meet the Israelis on condition the talks tackled the issues of Jewish settlements and Jerusalem and only after receiving U.S. guarantees the meeting would lead to a halt in settlement activities.
But Israeli officials said the meeting would deal with a different agenda.

Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel said: "In principle Israel didn't break off the talks, and we will raise issues that are of concern to us such as fighting terror and Palestinian violations to the agreement."

"We're not going to stop building in Jerusalem, we're not going to stop the natural growth of Jewish settlements," he said in the face of Palestinian assertions the Jewish settlements on occupied Arab lands are a provocation.

Political negotiations have been largely stalled since the start of the Jewish settlement construction and an attack on a Tel Aviv cafe in March that killed a Palestinian bomber and three Israelis women.
Palestinians refuse to resume the talks until settlement activities are halted.
